utility.notes: Clean Power Alliance's own notice to Sierra Madre residents compares its rates against 'SCE's default rate' and directs CARE/FERA enrollment 'through SCE by calling 800-798-5723 or visiting sce.com/care' — consistent with SCE remaining the delivery/billing utility while CPA supplies generation (see generation_supplier).

value.name: Clean Power Alliance (CPA) - 100% Green Power (default since October 2020)
value.notes: Per Clean Power Alliance's own co-branded notice with the City of Sierra Madre: 'Clean Power Alliance has been the electricity provider for the City of Sierra Madre since 2019... As of October 2020, Sierra Madre residents and businesses are receiving 100% Green Power (100% renewable energy) as their default rate product. The Sierra Madre City Council voted in February 2020 to adopt Clean Power Alliance's 100% Green Power as the default rate.' Customers may switch to CPA's Lean Power (36% renewable) or Clean Power (50% renewable) tiers at no cost.

county.notes: Confirmed by the U.S. Census Bureau's QuickFacts page, titled 'Sierra Madre city, California; Los Angeles County, California.'

permit_authority.value: City of Sierra Madre Planning & Community Preservation Department, Building Division

permit_url.notes: This is the City of Sierra Madre's own hosted 'Residential Solar Plan Check Submittal Checklist' (letterhead: 'CITY OF SIERRA MADRE, Planning & Community Preservation Department, 232 W. Sierra Madre Boulevard, Sierra Madre, CA 91204, Phone (626) 355.7138'), directly read and confirmed this session. Found via a search that initially suggested it was a Mountain View, CA document (the two cities share the same third-party CDN host, civiclive.com) — the actual document content was read in full before use and confirmed to belong to Sierra Madre, not Mountain View.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact (same URL applies to every city in SCE's distribution territory, including Sierra Madre), already established for the Irvine and Fullerton records this session. sce.com returned a DNS-level failure to automated fetch; the URL is confirmed to exist under this exact title on SCE's own domain via search engine indexing.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Sierra Madre/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for the PG&E-territory records and for Irvine/Fullerton (SCE); the general-market tier's own eligibility text directly names both PG&E and SCE customers.

value.name: Three sets of plans, including site/plot plan
Manufacturer specification sheets, installation instructions, and U.L. listings attached to the plans
Plans signed by a State of California licensed contractor (classification A, B, C-46, or C-10), licensed electrical engineer, or licensed architect, with signature and license number on each sheet
Owner's name and address on all plan sheets, specific to the project
Signed and dated 'Structural Guideline for Plan Check Submittal on Solar Panel Support' form
Roof plan showing location/dimensions of PV equipment and arrays, partial roof framing plan (rafter/beam/header size, span, spacing), roofing materials, and support/flashing details
Electrical drawings (2007 CEC compliance), single line diagram, inverter information, PV module information, and required system labels/warnings per NEC Article 690

required_documents.notes: From the City of Sierra Madre Building Division's 'Residential Solar Plan Check Submittal Checklist' (revised October 8, 2019).

value: One inspection is required for small residential rooftop solar energy systems eligible for expedited review, performed by the Building Division
Inspection is scheduled within two (2) business days of a request
Do not connect the solar voltaic system to the main power supply until after final approval by the city inspector

timeline_days.notes: The checklist states plan check review applies to 'small residential rooftop installations less than 10KW (kilowatts) in size' as 'approximate,' without giving a specific number of business/calendar days for plan review itself (distinct from the 2-business-day inspection-scheduling window, which is recorded under inspection_steps) — left null rather than substituting one concept for the other.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar (Building Division expedited review)
other_conditions: Applies to 'small residential rooftop installations less than 10KW (kilowatts) in size' — source did not specify AC vs. DC

No engineer's report/calculation required if: existing roofing material weighs 4 lb/sq ft or less (max 2 layers asphalt shingle or composition roofing); existing roof rafter/joist span does not exceed specified limits (e.g. 2x4 at 24" o.c. up to 6'-11", 2x6 at 16" o.c. up to 12'-6"); and the solar module/mounting system's distribution weight does not exceed 3 lb/sq ft

Property owner must install and maintain a metering system enabling compliance with the City of Sierra Madre's tax on cogenerated electricity (Sierra Madre Municipal Code Section 3.36.060) — a local municipal tax distinct from any building permit fee, with tax collected monthly and remitted by the property owner

eligibility_constraints.notes: The cogenerated-electricity tax (Municipal Code 3.36.060) is a genuinely distinctive, verified local requirement not seen in other cities' records this session — included as a condition since it directly affects solar system owners, not as a permit_fees entry since it is legally a tax, not a permit fee.

value.role: City of Sierra Madre Building Official, Planning & Community Preservation Department

official_contacts.notes: SGIP's own Contact page, directly fetched this session, lists an email (SGIPGroup@sce.com) and mailing address for SCE's SGIP administrator but explicitly no phone number — unlike PG&E's listing on the same page, which includes one.
